answer.rationale: Rollback is prohibited by compliance. Regional failover is high-risk at peak settlement traffic with heavy writes. Circuit breakers address partner dependency failures, not internal write-path latency. Adding capacity is slow and the root cause appears to be load-related, not capacity exhaustion per se. Memory b5 documents that routing report/read queries to replicas successfully relieved primary write-path pressure during a similar high-write scenario, and transactional latency recovered the same day. Since settlement traffic is at daily peak and the write path is 5x latency, the most likely lever is removing competing read load (dashboards, reporting, reconciliation queries) from the primary so write throughput can recover. This preserves all customer writes, requires no rollback, and is low-risk. I select memory_b5 for archive verification because it is the closest analog to this situation (write-path saturation, read load as contributor) and the intervention I intend depends on the specific mechanism it describes. If verification reveals a material discrepancy, I would shift to add_capacity as the fallback for the next window.
